sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's dive into processing 2D arrays! Think of them like spreadsheets or game boards where you can work with rows and columns.

• How to access and modify elements in 2D arrays
• Ways to loop through all elements efficiently
• Practical examples like finding sums or patterns

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a chessboard. Each square has a row and column number, right? A 2D array works the same way!

• It's just an array of arrays (rows containing columns)
• You use two indices: `array[row][column]`
• Great for grids, tables, or any data with two dimensions

For example, a 3x3 tic-tac-toe board would be a 2D array where you can check each cell for X, O, or empty. Simple!

steps.title: Access an Element

steps.title: Loop Through All Elements
steps.description: Use nested loops to visit every cell. The outer loop goes through rows, the inner loop through columns.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ 2D arrays are arrays of arrays (rows and columns)
✓ Nested loops are perfect for processing all elements
✓ Great for grids, tables, and game boards

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use `array[row].length` for column count in that row
donts: Don't assume all rows have the same number of columns
Don't forget to check array bounds
Don't confuse row and column order
sections.protip: For large 2D arrays, consider using enhanced for-loops for cleaner code!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Processing Two-Dimensional Arrays used in real apps?

examples.how: Each cell is an element in a 2D array. Formulas process rows/columns to calculate sums, averages, etc.
Pixels are stored in 2D arrays. Filters (like blur) process each pixel and its neighbors.
Game boards (chess, tic-tac-toe) or maps use 2D arrays to track positions and movements.

problem.description: Write a method that finds the sum of all elements in a 2D array. For example, given `{{1, 2}, {3, 4}}`, it should return `10`.
hints: Use nested loops to visit every element
Add each element to a running total
Don't forget to initialize the total to 0!
problem.explanation: We loop through each row and column, adding every element to `total`. The outer loop handles rows, and the inner loop handles columns.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 2D arrays are grids with rows and columns
📌 Use nested loops to process all elements
📌 Practice with real-world examples like spreadsheets or games
📌 Ready to move on to passing 2D arrays to methods!
